_comment: Vendored governance profile for the ASB (Agent Security Bench) benchmark. It is the deny-by-default tool allowlist + Airlock RASP config of a governed 'autonomous ops agent', EXTENDED with two fields the injection-defense profile did not need: `tool_reversibility` (the R1-R3 reversibility ladder classification per tool) and `budget.has_headroom` (whether the R2 budget gate has room). BOTH the Rust real-policy harness (rust/crates/fd-policy/tests/asb_defense.rs) and the fd-evals module (fd_evals.asb) read this exact file, so the enforcement decision is measured against one config on both planes. Airlock runs in enforce mode. The point of this profile vs. injection-defense: several tools are ALLOWLISTED but IRREVERSIBLE (deploy, apply_migration, rotate_credentials) — a backdoored plan that calls one is stopped not by the allowlist but by the graduated R3 rung (irreversible -> require_approval -> not auto-executed). That is the class of attack AgentDojo does not cover.

budget._comment: The R2 rung (allow_under_budget) only proceeds while the run's budget gate has headroom. Held true for this measurement so a benign `costly` tool executes; the R2->R3 escalation-on-exhaustion is unit-tested in fd_policy::reversibility, not in this corpus.

art50._comment: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations the enforcement plane requires on a generative response (fd_policy::transparency_art50). A response missing a required obligation is denied in enforce mode.
